commands: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user cohesivity https://cohesivity.ai/mcp/manage

commands: git clone --single-branch https://github.com/starsinc1708/teleloom.git && cd teleloom && uv sync --frozen && uv run teleloom init

name: Rufflet/mysql-legacy-mcp
description: Lets an agent inspect schema and run SELECT on local MySQL 5.0–5.6 by default, with opt-in INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/table-level DDL; live-verified against MySQL 5.0–8.0. Install: `npx -y mysql-legacy-mcp`. Transport: stdio. Auth: none at the MCP layer; MySQL login via env `MYSQL_LEGACY_HOST`, `MYSQL_LEGACY_USER`, `MYSQL_LEGACY_PASSWORD` (required), `MYSQL_LEGACY_DATABASE` optional. Clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code. Docs: https://github.com/Rufflet/mysql-legacy-mcp/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md. License: MIT. No public remote endpoint. Tools (11): mysql_legacy_ping, mysql_legacy_select, mysql_legacy_list_databases, mysql_legacy_list_tables, mysql_legacy_describe_table, mysql_legacy_show_create_table, mysql_legacy_list_indexes, mysql_legacy_insert, mysql_legacy_update, mysql_legacy_delete, mysql_legacy_ddl.

notes: Connects to the configured MySQL-compatible database using the supplied environment variables.

Supports Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Cursor. MIT.

commands: git clone https://github.com/scoretracker4321/json-mcp-lite && cd json-mcp-lite && npm install

name: ashishsinha1602/schemagate
description: Permission-aware schema access for text-to-SQL agents: picks the few tables a question needs and removes every table and column the caller's roles may not read before the model sees the schema; `run_query` also refuses them (quoted, bracketed, comma joins, `SELECT *`). Optional hash-chained, ML-DSA-65-signed audit log. Postgres, Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite. Install: one line with uv, `uvx --from "schemagate[mcp]" schemagate-mcp --url demo` (`demo` runs a built-in sample schema); for a database set `SCHEMAGATE_DATABASE_URL` and add its driver extra, e.g. `schemagate[mcp,postgres]`. Transport: stdio and streamable HTTP. Auth: none at the MCP layer; database credentials in the URL. Public demo endpoint (sample schema, no auth): `https://147-224-254-131.sslip.io/mcp`. Tools (7): select_schema, list_objects, describe_object, run_query, answer, refresh_catalog, health. Clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code. License: Apache-2.0. Official MCP Registry id `io.github.ashishsinha1602/schemagate`.

name: codegiveness/postgresql-sharp-mcp

Tools: `list_databases`, `list_schemas`, `list_objects`, `get_object_details`, `execute_sql`, `explain_query`, `analyze_indexes`, `get_top_queries`, `analyze_db_health`. Install: `npx -y --allow-scripts=@codegiveness/postgresql-sharp-mcp @codegiveness/postgresql-sharp-mcp@0.4.0` or `dotnet tool install --global codegiveness.postgresql-sharp-mcp`. Transport: stdio; auth: a PostgreSQL connection string in `POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING`. MIT.

Transport: stdio (`tirith stdio`) or Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:7477/mcp`, with a live dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:7477/`; local daemon, no auth, no telemetry, no embeddings. Clients: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, LangGraph, CrewAI, or any MCP client. Install: `cargo install tirith-mcp` (crate `tirith-mcp`, binary `tirith`), or prebuilt macOS, Linux and Windows binaries for x86_64 and ARM64 via `curl -LsSf https://eabz.github.io/tirith/install.sh | sh`. Five tools work with no account at all - what the broker does and what it costs, how to get a key, a preview of the live board, any agent's public reputation record, and the marketplace's aggregate stats - and with a key an agent can read its balance and escrow holds, negotiation threads, sealed deals and reveal packages, and rate a counterparty. name: jakegu1/vetagent
description: Pre-trade token check for AI agents that asks whether you could still sell. Sell simulation and buy/sell tax (Ethereum, BSC, Base), mint/freeze authority and holder concentration (Solana), liquidity depth, pair age and same-ticker impersonation, returned as one `low`/`medium`/`high`/`unknown` verdict with the signals behind it. Fail-closed: when a critical check cannot run it answers `unknown`, never low, and `low` means the exit was open when checked, not that nobody can close it. Publishes its measured error rates with the benchmark harness that reproduces them. Read-only: executes no trades, gives no investment advice. Remote Streamable HTTP endpoint `https://vetagent.dev/mcp` (no auth), plus plain HTTP `POST https://vetagent.dev/assess`. Official MCP Registry id `dev.vetagent/vetagent`. Free, no signup. MIT.

Agents can manage story projects, read and search continuity context, update locked canon, record approved scenes, save checkpoints, and run continuity checks. Hosted Streamable HTTP at `https://continuitywriter.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1; Pro plan or trial required. [Docs](https://github.com/LAHutchins91/continuity-mcp).

notes: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; no API key is required.

license: proprietary hosted service, source is not public

name: ssap-pa/self-learning-agent-setup
description: `feedback-memory` turns your approve, edit and reject decisions into memory an agent checks before it drafts: `record_decision` saves the edit and your reason, `recall_corrections` returns the closest past corrections and standing rules for the next task. Five tools (`recall_corrections`, `record_decision`, `add_rule`, `list_memory`, `forget`); local Postgres + pgvector via PGlite in `~/.feedback-memory`, offline hashing embedder by default or OpenAI embeddings when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set. Install: `claude mcp add feedback-memory -- npx -y github:ssap-pa/self-learning-agent-setup`. Transport: `stdio`; no auth; clients: Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, and compatible MCP clients. MIT. In-browser demo: https://ssap-pa.github.io/self-learning-agent-setup/.

commands: claude mcp add feedback-memory -- npx -y github:ssap-pa/self-learning-agent-setup

name: uNotes
description: Search a library of university course materials (past exams, assignments, lab reports, lecture notes) and your uNotes flashcards and quizzes. Hosted remote endpoint: `https://unotes.net/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, no API key). Official MCP Registry: `net.unotes/unotes`. Setup for Cursor, VS Code, Cline and Claude Code: https://github.com/DevinoSolutions/mcp-servers/tree/main/unotes

name: Save This One

notes: Add the remote endpoint in an OAuth-capable client and complete the browser sign-in.

license: Proprietary hosted service; no public source repository or installable package is being submitted.

Exposes `convert_pdf_to_markdown` so agents can read documents for RAG, notes, or analysis. Install with `npx -y @happywp/pdftomarkdown-mcp`; stdio transport with `PDFTOMARKDOWN_API_KEY`. MIT.

notes: api-key

name: volcengine/OpenViking
description: Self-hosted context database for AI agents (39k+ GitHub stars) — resources, memory and skills in one browsable `viking://` filesystem with layered L0/L1/L2 summaries, exposed to coding agents over MCP. Install: `uv tool install openviking --upgrade` then `openviking-server init`. Transport: streamable HTTP at `http://<server>:1933/mcp`. Clients: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode. AGPL-3.0. Site: https://openviking.ai/.

name: Selvedge
description: Record and retrieve coding decisions, reasons, and rejected approaches by entity across agent sessions in a local SQLite database. Install: `uv tool install selvedge`; launch: `selvedge-server`. Transport: stdio. Auth: none. Clients: compatible local stdio MCP clients, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code, and Windsurf. Tools: 8, including `log_change`, `prior_attempts`, `blame`, and `stale_decisions`. License: MIT. Docs: https://selvedge.sh/start/what-is-selvedge/.

notes: The local stdio server requires no API key or hosted account.
Metadata follows Selvedge v0.3.16 server.json, pyproject.toml, and selvedge/server.py.
Requires uv. Use a supported Python release (3.11–3.14); the package also accepts Python 3.10 for compatibility.
SELVEDGE_DB is optional. Set it to the absolute path of the project's .selvedge/selvedge.db when the client starts outside the project. See the quickstart for initialization and agent instructions.

name: MemTether
description: Local cross-client memory hub with a tamper-evident evidence chain, supersession history, conflict detection, and adapters for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Gemini CLI, and other clients. Install with `pip install memtether`, then run `memtether init` to create the local database and configure detected clients. Apache-2.0.

name: ORANO
description: Hosted, read-only memory of what you saved: projects ORANO builds from Reels, TikToks, YouTube videos, articles and PDFs (summaries, key takeaways, ordered tasks, research), selectable video context (transcript, on-screen text, sampled frames, links) and curated memory facts. Tools: `list_projects`, `get_project`, `get_project_context`, `get_pending_handoffs`, `search_library`, `get_memory_facts`. Endpoint: `https://orano-ai-backend-1037939693300.us-central1.run.app/mcp/`. Transport: streamable HTTP. Auth: bearer personal API key (`orano:read`, ORANO MCP web plan). Manifest: https://github.com/infotik/orano-mcp-server.

name: Remnant Read
description: Search prior technical agent experience and inspect its published evidence, applicability conditions, failed approaches, and reported outcomes before trying a solution. The anonymous Read connection is read-only; recording outcomes and contributing reusable lessons use a separate authenticated connection. Hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint: `https://remnant.dedale-bi.com/mcp/chatgpt`; no authentication. Seven tools include `search_memories`, `inspect_memory`, and trust-passport inspection. [Setup](https://github.com/Dedale-Project/remnant-connect/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPER_QUICKSTART.md).
license: No open-source license granted for the repository; the hosted backend is not published in this repository.

name: agents-learning
description: Local project memory for Codex: search bounded knowledge previews and read revision-aware pages with applicability, limits and source evidence. Uses Python stdio MCP, SQLite and FTS, with optional local semantic retrieval. The full plugin adds lifecycle Hooks; administrator review and trusted publication use separate roles.

name: Enhanciar
description: Hosted remote MCP server for a team's company brain. Ask questions over connected Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Jira, Linear and GitHub and get answers with a link to every source; tools include `query`, `search_wiki`, `get_page`, `impact` (code change impact) and `propose_action`, which queues a drafted reply, ticket or doc for a person to approve. Endpoint: `https://enhanciar.in/enhanciar/mcp/`. Transport: `streamable-http`; auth: bearer API key (`dh_...`, created in the app). Clients: Claude Code, Claude Desktop (via `mcp-remote`), Cursor, VS Code, and compatible remote-MCP clients. Site: https://enhanciar.in. Docs: https://enhanciar.in/mcp. Official Registry: `in.enhanciar/enhanciar`. Paid service; docs repo MIT.

name: Folio Wiki
description: Open-source (MIT) self-hosted wiki for teams in which every page is a Markdown file in a Git repository, with a built-in MCP server. Its 23 tools cover search, reading, creating and editing pages, data tables, whiteboards and page history. Install: Docker image `ghcr.io/evergreen-it-dev/folio` (docker compose). Transport: Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` on your own instance; auth: OAuth 2.1 or personal access token. Clients: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and other HTTP-transport MCP clients. TypeScript, MIT. Site: https://foliowiki.online. Docs: https://github.com/evergreen-it-dev/folio/blob/main/docs/MCP.md. Official Registry: `io.github.evergreen-it-dev/folio`.

name: Pinto Notes
description: Hosted MCP server for Pinto Notes, a free, open-source notes app for Mac (iPhone in progress) that imports Apple Notes. Lets an agent search, read, create and edit notes, tick checklist items and add rows to tables, and every change keeps the previous version. Endpoint: `https://mcp.pintonotes.com`. Transport: `streamable-http`; auth: OAuth, approved by the person in the app, read only or read and edit. Clients: ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and other remote MCP clients. Server source in `supabase/functions/mcp`, TypeScript, MIT. Site: https://pintonotes.com. Docs: https://pintonotes.com/blog/mcp-server. Official Registry: `com.pintonotes/pinto-notes`.

name: ilyautov/moysklad-mcp-ru
description: MoySklad, a widely used Russian trade-management and inventory service, for AI agents: stock, products, orders, counterparties, stores, profit/turnover/cash reports, and document writes. 892 methods from the official JSON API 1.2 docs ship as a catalog the server executes, reached through 8 generic meta-tools (`ms_search_methods`, `ms_describe_method`, `ms_call_method`, `ms_call_raw`, `ms_fetch_all`, `ms_map` plus cabinet tools) alongside typed read tools, so a client sees tool slots instead of 892 schemas. Every method is classified read / write / destructive: reads run immediately, creating a document needs `confirm_write=true` and `MOYSKLAD_ALLOW_WRITE=1`, and posting or deleting additionally needs `i_understand_this_modifies_data=true`; creating always produces a draft and posting is a separate step, enforced by a CI test that no mutation is labelled read. 7 document role types (purchaseorder, supply, demand, invoicein, invoiceout, salesreturn, purchasereturn). API amounts are in kopecks and read tools convert to rubles. Auto-pagination, multiple cabinets, Russian-language catalog search. Install: `uvx moysklad-mcp-ru`; stdio; token from MoySklad Settings -> Users -> Access tokens, stored locally at `~/.moysklad-mcp/cabinets.json` (chmod 600). Clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode. Method map and setup: https://moysklad-mcp-ru.aifrontier.tech/ . Official MCP Registry id `io.github.ilyautov/moysklad-mcp-ru`. Alpha: the curated core and the write slice are verified against a live cabinet, the rest of the catalog is imported from the docs. MIT.

Transport: Streamable HTTP via Apify, using the actor-specific URL in the setup docs; auth: OAuth with the caller's own Apify account or an Apify API token, and the caller's account is billed per result, so there is no key to buy from the publisher. Measured: a Google Maps search that returns 160 places returns 766 with adaptive map-grid splitting; reading contact pages as well as the home page found an email on 57 of 135 live business websites against 31 from the home page alone; an OpenStreetMap sweep of Austin, Texas returned 7,673 named businesses of which 3,932 have no website. name: stephen1137/phpray

Always-on request tracing: every request a site serves is stored with wall time, CPU, memory, SQL queries as fingerprints with the literals stripped, outbound HTTP calls, PHP errors and N+1 patterns; a sample adds per-plugin time attribution. 10 read-only tools: site list, overview, slowest pages, slowest queries, component breakdown, errors, trace search, one trace end to end, before/after compare, and live alerts. The hosted endpoint answers with **no key** from a read-only demo account holding real WooCommerce traffic, so the tools can be tried before installing anything. Runs where PHP usually runs — the extension loads from your own `php.ini` and the WordPress plugin needs neither an extension nor a daemon, so shared hosting without root works. Install: `claude mcp add --transport http phpray https://phpray.dev/mcp`. Transport: `http` (bearer console token, optional) or `stdio`. Registry id `dev.phpray/phpray`. Go/C, Apache-2.0.

name: TheDeskMonitor
description: AI-infused workforce productivity MCP server for live team questions: who is clocked in, productivity scores, timesheet summaries, payroll cost per person, pending approvals, and workload alerts. Remote Streamable HTTP endpoint with OAuth 2.1 / PKCE plus API-key demo mode.

notes: OAuth 2.1 / PKCE plus API-key support. Demo mode is available with dm_demo_* keys.
Health, tools, and OpenAPI discovery endpoints were provided in issue #1419.

name: 2nd1st/open-mcp-apps
description: MCP Apps engine for persistent, reusable UI. The AI writes a single-file HTML app — todo board, habit tracker, dashboard, reading list — against a small `window.oma` API, saves it to a registry, and reopens it by name in any later chat. Data lives in generic collections backed by SQLite plus an append-only change ledger, so it outlives the conversation and the AI and the human edit the same store; every mutation is an idempotent command with optimistic concurrency. Ships a 22-app App Store with live previews and one-click install. 33 tools. Transport: stdio. Auth: none (runs locally). Registers into Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex; apps render in any MCP Apps-capable host (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Codex, ChatGPT). Requires Node 22+. Install: `npx -y @2nd1st/open-mcp-apps`. License: MIT. Hosted version at https://openmcp.app.

name: Odrin/rhizome-mcp
description: Durable, local-first project coordination for autonomous coding agents across sessions and agent products. Agents can create and prioritize issues, manage labels and dependency graphs, claim work with renewable leases, save checkpoints, record decisions and comments, search project history, coordinate review requests, and recover after crashes or context limits.

name: Wagglet
description: Prepared-task handoff between a human teammate and their own coding agent - read the authorized ticket or Story, then move it with explicit lifecycle commands (claim, deliver, review) instead of free-form status writes, using a fresh operation id per mutation. Transport: streamable HTTP. Auth: personal MCP token; a token names one connection and never overrides that person's current Team roles or permissions, and Team-level MCP access is off by default. Docs URL: https://wagglet.com/docs/mcp.

name: edouard-claude/redmine-mcp
description: Redmine over MCP — read and write issues, comments and attachments, browse projects, manage users, groups and memberships. Every write is confirmed by a human through MCP elicitation before it reaches the API, and fails closed on a decline or a timeout. Go, single static binary.

name: com.cogram/project
description: Read an architecture or engineering firm's projects, meetings, emails, RFIs, submittals, drawings, field reports and transmittals. Read-only; cannot create, change or delete Cogram records. Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.cogram.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1 and a Cogram account.

notes: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. Requires a Cogram account; the agent sees exactly what the connecting user can see.

name: azimov777/casefile
description: The task tracker your AI agents keep for each other — each task carries a case file of decisions, failed attempts, findings, and open questions, so the next agent with a fresh context picks up where the last one stopped. A live web board lets a human watch progress, answer questions, and leave remarks. Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azimov777/casefile/main/install.sh | sh`. Transport: streamable HTTP. Auth: bearer token per agent. License: MIT.

name: GTD Brain
description: Getting Things Done board that ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients can run for you: capture to Inbox, next actions by context, projects, waiting-for and weekly review. 16 tools and 4 prompts. Endpoint: `https://mcp.gtdbrain.com/api/gtdbrain/v1/mcp`. Transport: streamable-http. Auth: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE, sign in with an email code, no token to paste. Docs URL: https://gtdbrain.com/connect. Free allowance, then subscription. Official MCP Registry id: `com.gtdbrain/gtd-brain`.

name: DokuTrak
description: Collect documents from your clients without leaving your agent. Create a DokuTrak document request (the email to the client goes out only after you confirm), see where a request stands file by file with each verdict and the reminder state, chase the client on rejected files, and download the collected files as a ZIP. Approving or rejecting a file is never a tool: it stays with the professional. 4 tools. Install: `npx -y dokutrak-mcp`. Transport: stdio. Auth: API key (`DOKUTRAK_API_KEY`, issued from Settings → Connect an agent in DokuTrak). Clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code. License: MIT. Official MCP Registry id: `io.github.Crackx17/dokutrak-mcp`.

name: WebAsk MCP

commands: claude mcp add --transport http webask https://mcp.webask.io/mcp/v1 --header "Authorization: Bearer $WEBASK_API_KEY"

notes: api-key; send the required Authorization request header with a Bearer token from the user's own WebAsk API key. Create the key under Settings > API / MCP in WebAsk.

license: MIT (repository docs, configs, and skills); hosted WebAsk service is proprietary

notes: Repository, documentation, license, and hosted endpoint authentication response were checked during maintainer review.
Metadata updated from issue #2880. Source: https://github.com/WebAskio/webask-mcp/blob/main/en/README.md https://webask.io/dev/api/mcp

name: zerx-lab/FluxDown

name: bitterdev/pdf-letter-mcp
description: Turns a structured letter into a print ready PDF laid out to DIN 5008, so the recipient block lands exactly in the window of a DL or C6/C5 envelope instead of half behind the paper. Runs entirely offline with no external API. Reusable sender profiles, English and German fixed texts and salutations, subject and reference blocks, and a signature image that gets background-stripped and scaled. Pairs with pixelletter-mcp, which posts the file it writes. 7 tools including `create_letter`, `preview_letter`, `prepare_signature` and `get_din5008_spec`. Transport: stdio. Auth: none. License: MIT. Install: `npx -y pdf-letter-mcp`.

name: ai-detect
description: Local AI-text detection scored sentence by sentence with a DeBERTa-v3-large model that ranked first on the RAID benchmark. Explains why each line reads as machine-written - missing contractions, formal verbs, "Furthermore" openers - and suggests a rewrite. Runs offline after the first model download; no API key, nothing leaves your machine. Install: `pip install .`. MIT.

name: Identik-me/identik-mcp
description: Argentine electronic and digital signature (Ley 25.506) through Identik — list templates, create a document from a template, send it out for signature, track status, resend invitations, download the signed PDF with its audit certificate, fetch the audit trail, and cryptographically verify a signed PDF (integrity, certificate chain, RFC-3161 timestamp). Two remote Streamable HTTP endpoints: `https://electronica.identik.me/api/mcp` (electronic signature) and `https://firma.identik.me/api/mcp` (digital signature with licensed-CA certificates). Bearer API-token auth; published in the official MCP registry as `me.identik/electronica` and `me.identik/firma`. Sandbox environments available for evaluation.

name: alex-zwingli/plan-to-eat-mcp
description: Unofficial client for a personal [Plan to Eat](https://www.plantoeat.com) account — the meal-planning app. Recipe book CRUD (create from a URL or a payload, browse courses, cuisines and tags), the weekly planner (schedule recipes, prep notes and ingredient entries; move, duplicate, reorder within a slot, rescale servings, check for duplicates before scheduling), leftovers as a first-class flow, freezer portion tracking, and the shopping list Plan to Eat generates from the plan. 30 tools. A `plan-to-eat` CLI ships from the same tool registry, so the two surfaces cannot drift. Transport: stdio. Auth: `PLAN_TO_EAT_USERNAME` / `PLAN_TO_EAT_PASSWORD` env vars; the server logs in and caches the cookie session to disk. Clients: Claude Code (ships as a plugin with two skills), Claude Desktop, Cursor, and any stdio MCP host. License: MIT. Requires Node 18+. Install: `npx -y plan-to-eat-mcp` (or `npm i -g plan-to-eat-mcp`; the CLI is the `plan-to-eat` bin from the same package).

name: ToolsMonk
description: Catalog lookup over 255 free browser-based tools in 10 categories (PDF, image, text, SEO, developer, calculators and everyday utilities), so an agent can find the right tool for a described task and hand back its URL. Read-only: it returns tool pages and does not upload, process or convert files. Five tools (`search_tools`, `get_tool`, `list_tools`, `list_categories`, `get_site_info`) plus 3 resources; ranked search accepts plain-language tasks such as "compress a PDF under 2MB". Streamable HTTP endpoint: `https://toolsmonk.com/api/mcp`. No auth, no API key, free, 120 requests/min per IP. Docs: https://toolsmonk.com/developers/mcp. Registry id `com.toolsmonk/catalog`.

name: Qty
description: Deterministic quantity tools for agents. Nine tools: `convert` and `units` are free; `parse` (messy quantity text such as 5'11" or 2x4x8 ft), `batch`, `receipt`, `compare-prices`, `scale-recipe`, `size` (shoe and clothing sizes) and `date` are paid per call with exact USDC via x402 on Base or Solana ($0.001-$0.01). Never invents a number: unknown amounts return null with a reason. Streamable HTTP endpoint: `https://qty.vercel.app/mcp`. No account or API key. Docs: https://qty.vercel.app/llms.txt.

name: Winters Works Domain WHOIS
description: WHOIS-style domain lookups over official RDAP, so an agent gets registrar, created and expiry dates, days until expiry, nameservers, DNSSEC and EPP status, and whether a name looks available to register. 3 tools (`lookup_domain`, `lookup_domains` for up to 50 at once, `check_availability`), optional live DNS check (A, MX, SPF). Transport: Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.apify.com?actors=wintersworks/domain-whois-mcp-server`. Auth: Apify OAuth or API token. Pay per use, $0.002 per domain looked up; failed lookups are free. Registry id `io.github.winters-works-co/domain-whois`.
